errors: No mathematical content on this page, so there are no mathematical errors here.

Context note on the next page: in modern counts, the unique fundamental solution that is symmetric (invariant under 180° rotation) has only 4 distinct variants, not 8. The next page's claim of '8 Varianten' is therefore doubtful, unless the writer counted differently.

results.what: Archival label for enclosed material on the eight queens problem (a later copy, not in Gauss's hand, donated by Frau Listing in 1868)
results.modern_name: Eight queens problem (only the title appears)
results.usually_credited_to: Posed by Max Bezzel (1848); first complete solution count of 92 by Franz Nauck (1850); Gauss discussed it in letters to Schumacher (1850)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a cover/wrapper sheet with only archival and provenance notes. It is explicitly marked as not in Gauss's hand, and Gauss's interest in the eight queens problem is well documented through his correspondence with Schumacher.

checkable.asserts: Context only, not on this page: the 92 solutions of the eight queens problem arise from 12 fundamental solutions. Eleven of these have 8 symmetry variants each, and the single symmetric one has 4.
